history.origins: Originating in the AustrondHungarian Empire, the name 'Ferbli' (or Färbeln) is derived from the German word 'Farbe' (suit). The earliest recorded prohibition of the game dates back to 1714, suggesting it was already a significant gambling game by the early 18th century.
timeline: 1714: First historical reference in German gaming prohibitions.
1800s: Becomes a social sensation in Hungarian high society and urban cafes.
Early 20th Century: Replaced by Poker in many cities but preserved in rural areas.
Present: Still played in specialized circles in Hungary and Transylvania.
history.cultural: In Hungarian literature and cinema, Ferbli is often depicted as the quintessential game of rural gentry and high-stakes social competition.
history.evolution: The game moved from a three-card variant (Färbeln) to a four-card variant (Ferbli), introducing more complex betting patterns and wild card variations.

setup.deck: 32-card German deck (William Tell design). Suits: Acorns, Leaves, Bells (Gourds), Hearts.
setup.dealing: Each player is dealt 4 cards in two batches of two. Dealing a- play proceed counterclockwise.

rules.objective: Win the pot either by having the best four-card ha- or by bluffing opponents into folding.
rules.gameplay: Players are dealt 4 cards in two batches. Betting proceeds with players able to bet, call, or fold. The strongest hands are Four of a Kind and the Banda (four cards of same suit). The hand rankings follow a hierarchy similar to Poker but adapted for the 32-card deck.
keyRules: Play Again: If only one player bets and no one calls, they take the pot without showing.
Positions: In a tie of hand rank and value, the player closest to the dealer's right (the 'Mano' or lead) wins because they had to act first.
Aces (Pigs): The Ace is the highest-value card both in rank and points (11).

strategy.basic: Prioritize suit gathering over rank sets initially. A 'Banda' (4 of a suit) is easier to build than 4 of a rank and beats almost everything else.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Vizi' Bluff: Players who bet heavily during the first two cards often signal a pair of Aces. If you have any Ace in hand, you know their 'Two Aces' hand is weakened.
strategy.advanced: Position Play: Since ties are broken by table position (counterndclockwise proximity to the lead), being the first player allows you to bluff more effectively because an opponent with an equal hand must fold to you.
tips: Don't be afraid to fold early if your first two cards are of different suits and low ranks.
